notYet: Not yet part of the Near East

stages.name: Beyond Assyria's reach
stages.desc: Independent kingdoms and peoples: Lydia, Phrygia, Urartu, the Cimmerians

stages.name: Assyrian vassals
stages.desc: Local kings who swear oaths and pay tribute to Assyria

stages.name: Rebels allied with Kush
stages.desc: Defying Assyria, with Kush's backing or in hope of it

stages.name: Kushite rule
stages.desc: Ruled by the Nubian pharaohs of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty

stages.name: Egyptian Delta princes
stages.desc: Local dynasts of Lower Egypt, installed or tolerated by Assyria

stages.name: Saite Egypt
stages.desc: Egypt reunited under Psamtik I of Sais, the Twenty-sixth Dynasty

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The kings of Cyprus have paid tribute since Sargon II set up his stele at Kition in 707 BC
Ten Cypriot kings appear on Esarhaddon's list of vassals sending timber and stone to Nineveh
Cypriot kings send ships and men for Ashurbanipal's march on Egypt

states.name: Israel
timeline: The Philistine kings of Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron are vassals; the north is the province of Megiddo
The Philistine coast is the staging ground for Esarhaddon's march on Egypt

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Judah under Manasseh and the city of Gaza pay tribute; Samaria is an Assyrian province
Manasseh of Judah is among the twenty-two kings who bring materials to Nineveh

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Sidon under Abdi-Milkutti and Tyre under Ba'al pay tribute to Assyria, as since 701 BC
Abdi-Milkutti of Sidon rises against Esarhaddon; Assyrian texts name a Cilician ally, and Egyptian encouragement is suspected but unproven
Sidon is razed; its land becomes the province of Kar-Esarhaddon, and part goes to Tyre
Ba'al of Tyre 'trusts in his friend Taharqa' and throws off the Assyrian yoke
Blockaded, Tyre comes to terms and loses its mainland towns; by 667 Ba'al sends ships for Assyria
Ba'al breaks with Assyria again as Tantamani retakes Egypt (the exact year is uncertain)
Ba'al submits to Ashurbanipal, sends his daughter and son to Nineveh, and keeps his throne

states.name: Syria
timeline: Damascus, Hamath and Arpad are Assyrian provinces; Arwad on the coast is a vassal kingdom
Assyrian armies march south through Syria toward Egypt
Yakinlu, king of Arwad, submits to Ashurbanipal

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Phrygia, Lydia, Urartu and Cimmerian raiders lie beyond Assyria; only Cilicia and Harran in the southeast are Assyrian provinces
Esarhaddon beheads Sanduarri of Kundu and Sissu in Cilicia, Sidon's ally
Gyges of Lydia seeks Assyria's help against the Cimmerians

states.name: Sudan
timeline: The heartland of Kush: Napata, Gebel Barkal, Kawa and the royal cemeteries
Taharqa is buried at Nuri; Tantamani is crowned at Napata and marches north
Kush keeps its own throne at Napata, south of Psamtik's frontier at Elephantine

states.name: Iraq
timeline: The Assyrian heartland of Nineveh, Ashur and Calah, with Babylonia under Assyrian kings
Sennacherib floods and destroys rebellious Babylon
Sennacherib is murdered by his sons; Esarhaddon wins the throne
Ashurbanipal rules at Nineveh, his brother Shamash-shum-ukin at Babylon

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Ammon, Moab and Edom pay tribute; the Arab tribes of the desert are courted and fought
Arab kings provide the camels that carry water for Esarhaddon's army across Sinai

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Taharqa, crowned at Memphis, rules the Nile from the Delta to beyond the Fourth Cataract
The Babylonian Chronicle records an Assyrian army defeated in Egypt
Esarhaddon takes Memphis; Delta princes rule as Assyrian-appointed kings
Taharqa returns and retakes Memphis; Esarhaddon dies marching back
Ashurbanipal's army drives Taharqa south; Necho of Sais and the princes are reinstated
Tantamani marches north and retakes Memphis; Necho of Sais dies, probably in the fighting
Assyria sacks Thebes; Psamtik of Sais holds the Delta as Assyria's client, while Thebes still dates its documents by Tantamani
Nitocris is adopted at Thebes: Psamtik I is recognised from the sea to Aswan

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: The kings of Cyprus have paid tribute since Sargon II set up his stele at Kition in 707 BC
Ten Cypriot kings appear on Esarhaddon's list of vassals sending timber and stone to Nineveh
Cypriot kings send ships and men for Ashurbanipal's march on Egypt

events.title: Taharqa crowned
events.text: After the death of Shebitku, Taharqa is crowned at Memphis, ruling from the Mediterranean to the upper Nile.

events.title: Babylon destroyed
events.text: Sennacherib sacks rebellious Babylon and floods the city with canals.

events.title: The great flood
events.text: In Taharqa's sixth year a high Nile brings a record harvest, celebrated on stelae from Kawa to the Delta.

events.title: Borrowed victories
events.text: Taharqa's temple at Kawa copies Old Kingdom scenes of a Libyan conquest, a royal boast not to be read as history.

events.title: Cedar for Kawa
events.text: Kawa's inscriptions record true cedar of Lebanon for the god's temple, a sign of Kush's reach into the Phoenician timber trade.

events.title: Sennacherib murdered
events.text: The Assyrian king is killed by his sons; Esarhaddon fights his way to the throne in Nineveh.

events.title: Colonnade at Karnak
events.text: Taharqa raises a vast columned kiosk in the first court of Amun's temple at Thebes.

events.title: Arza taken
events.text: Esarhaddon seizes Arza by the Brook of Egypt and deports its king, opening the road to the Nile.

events.title: Sidon falls
events.text: After Abdi-Milkutti's revolt, Esarhaddon captures Sidon, plunders it and tears down its walls.

events.title: King of Sidon beheaded
events.text: Abdi-Milkutti, caught after fleeing by sea, is beheaded; his head is paraded at Nineveh.

events.title: Cilician ally beheaded
events.text: Sanduarri, king of Kundu and Sissu and Sidon's ally, suffers the same fate.

events.title: Kar-Esarhaddon
events.text: A new Assyrian harbour town named for the king replaces Sidon, and settlers are brought from the east.

events.title: Treaty with Tyre
events.text: Ba'al of Tyre swears a treaty fixing Assyria's tolls, ports and rights over shipwrecks.

events.title: Repulsed from Egypt
events.text: The Babylonian Chronicle records an Assyrian army defeated in Egypt; Esarhaddon's own annals are silent.

events.title: Kings of Cyprus
events.text: Ten kings of Cyprus send timber and stone for Esarhaddon's arsenal at Nineveh.

events.title: Manasseh's tribute
events.text: Manasseh of Judah is listed among twenty-two vassal kings of the west.

events.title: Succession oaths
events.text: At Calah, vassals and officials swear to accept Ashurbanipal as heir; copies survive from as far as Tayinat.

events.title: Tyre defies Assyria
events.text: Ba'al of Tyre sides with Taharqa; Esarhaddon blockades the island city, cutting off food and water.

events.title: Camels across Sinai
events.text: Arab allies supply camels carrying water so the army can cross the desert from Raphia.

events.title: Memphis falls
events.text: Esarhaddon takes Memphis 'in half a day'; Taharqa, wounded, escapes, but his queen and son Ushanahuru are captured.

events.title: Governors for the Delta
events.text: Esarhaddon installs Delta princes, renames cities and imposes yearly tribute on Egypt.

events.title: Dog River inscription
events.text: Esarhaddon carves his victory beside those of Ramesses II at the mouth of the Nahr el-Kalb.

events.title: Victory stele
events.text: The stele of Sam'al shows Esarhaddon holding Taharqa's son, kneeling, on a rope through his lips.

events.title: Taharqa returns
events.text: Taharqa retakes Memphis, and Esarhaddon's appointees flee or change sides.

events.title: Esarhaddon dies
events.text: Marching back toward Egypt, Esarhaddon falls ill and dies at Harran.

events.title: Ashurbanipal crowned
events.text: Ashurbanipal takes the throne at Nineveh; his brother Shamash-shum-ukin rules Babylon.

events.title: Battle of Kar-Baniti
events.text: Ashurbanipal's army, with ships and men from twenty-two western kings, routs Taharqa's forces in the Delta.

events.title: Taharqa withdraws
events.text: Taharqa abandons Memphis and falls back to Thebes, then to Napata.

events.title: The princes' plot
events.text: Necho of Sais and two other princes are caught writing to Taharqa and are sent in chains to Nineveh.

events.title: Necho restored
events.text: Ashurbanipal pardons Necho and sends him back as king of Sais; his son Psamtik is given Athribis.

events.title: Gyges seeks Assyria
events.text: Gyges, king of Lydia, sends envoys to Nineveh seeking help against the Cimmerians.

events.title: Taharqa dies
events.text: Taharqa is buried at Nuri beneath the largest pyramid ever built for a Nubian king.

events.title: Tantamani's dream
events.text: His Dream Stela at Gebel Barkal tells how two serpents promised Tantamani the rule of the north and south.

events.title: Necho killed
events.text: Tantamani retakes Memphis; Necho of Sais dies, probably killed in the fighting, and Psamtik flees.

events.title: Psamtik's first year
events.text: Psamtik's later reign counts its years from this date, as heir of Sais under Assyrian protection.

events.title: Thebes sacked
events.text: Assyrian troops plunder Thebes and carry off two great obelisks; Egyptian sources say nothing.

events.title: Tantamani flees
events.text: Tantamani escapes south to Kipkipi, perhaps near Kom Ombo, and keeps his title in Thebes.

events.title: Tyre submits
events.text: Ba'al of Tyre yields to Ashurbanipal, sending his daughter and his son Yahimilki to Nineveh.

events.title: Arwad submits
events.text: Yakinlu, king of the island city of Arwad, bows to Ashurbanipal.

events.title: Bronze men from the sea
events.text: Herodotus says Ionian and Carian mercenaries in bronze armour won Psamtik his kingdom.

events.title: The Delta united
events.text: Psamtik subdues the rival princes and Libyan chiefs of the Delta, from Sais to Tanis.

events.title: Nitocris to Thebes
events.text: Psamtik's fleet brings his daughter Nitocris to Thebes, to be adopted as the next God's Wife of Amun.

events.title: Southern frontier
events.text: Upper Egypt recognises Psamtik; Kush withdraws behind the cataract at Aswan.

chartNote: Share of the area of eleven present-day countries, by who held each one. Regions are today's boundaries, and each is given one colour although many held a province, vassal cities and desert tribes at once. Sudan and Egypt are vast and swing the shares. Dates follow the Assyrian annals and chronicles and the Egyptian and Kushite stelae, which are often partisan and sometimes differ by a year.
